col1:
Hi, I'm Luis —
a Software Engineer focused on UX.
Currently working at Dell on the Dell Design System.

I'm an IT professional with deep expertise in web development, systems analysis, and project management. I specialize in building innovative, efficient digital solutions with a strong focus on SEO, accessibility, and performance. My programming background spans ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript, and SQL, alongside modern frameworks such as React, Vue, and Angular.
col2: I studied at UFSM (Federal University of Santa Maria) in Frederico Westphalen, Brazil, earning a degree in Technology for Internet Systems, followed by a postgraduate course in "Gestão de T.I" (IT Management) at UFSM.
My work is always focused on delivering pixel-perfect layouts — code that is easy to use, fast, beautiful, and smooth.

I love CSS animation. I spent years crafting Melissa's seasonal collections almost entirely in CSS, and have since worked with JS-based animations using Vue and Lottie, experimented with Three.js, and recently started exploring spec-driven development and AI.

sections: Focusing on sustainability, METCHA's project aimed to be carbon neutral. Using modern content delivery techniques — green distributed networks like Cloudflare, code splitting, and progressive loading — we served only the code needed by the UI in real-time, while maintaining 100% semantic HTML for accessibility and SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

col1:
Oi, sou o Luis —
Engenheiro de Software com foco em UX.
Trabalho na Dell no Dell Design System.

Trabalho com tecnologia faz tempo — desenvolvimento web, análise de sistemas e gestão de projetos. Gosto muito de criar coisas digitais eficientes, com atenção especial a SEO, acessibilidade e performance. Já trabalhei com ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript, SQL e frameworks como React, Vue e Angular.
col2: Me formei na UFSM (Universidade Federal de Santa Maria) em Frederico Westphalen — RS, em Tecnologia em Sistemas para Internet, com pós-graduação em Gestão de T.I. também pela UFSM.
No trabalho, me dedico muito a entregar layouts pixel-perfect — código limpo, rápido, bonito e fluido.

CSS e animação sempre foram minha praia. Passei anos criando as coleções da Melissa quase inteiramente em CSS. Depois passei pra animações em JS com Vue e Lottie, brinquei com Three.js e mais recentemente tô explorando desenvolvimento guiado por specs e IA.

Trabalhando na Transa, também desenvolvi uma série de landing pages dedicadas ao Fórum Anual do Couro CICB.
2017 trouxe uma nova edição: 'Economia Circular'.
A edição de 2018 foi intitulada 'Qual é o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.
A edição de 2019 foi intitulada 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.
2020 foi um desafio — duas edições foram criadas do zero: um fórum online chamado 'Leather Forward' e um evento presencial.
Essa edição foi intitulada 'Nosso ambiente em conexão'.
Criei o layout com base no layout anterior criado pelo Sagu, na Transa.
I contributed as a member of the team as a JR. Front-end developer, guided by Cristiano Becker on the development of this page in my first year at Transa.
2017 brought a new edition, 'Econômia Circular'.
It was developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2018' edition was called, 'Qual o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.
It was also developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for the CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
2019' edition was called, 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.
Developed using PHP, Jquery and CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/Subscription submitting of the application.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.
Both pages were developed using PHP, Sass for the CSS and Vanilla JS with code created from scratch exclusively for these new pages.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2021's edition brought a new challenge - creating the layout, and also coding the project.
This edition called:'Nosso ambiente em conexão'.
I created the webpage layout based on the previous layout created by Sagu, at Transa for the 2020 edition, keeping the already established visual identity.
The coding of the webpage was done in Vanilla JS, Sass(CSS3) and HTML5 only, with the use of lots of SVG elements in the layout of the page.

sections: Melissa's website was a project developed by TRANSA INC.
I worked on the project from 2016 to 2020, when the project was ended.
Initially as a Jr. Front end Developer, guided by Cristiano Becker and ended as a Full Front End Developer by the end of the project.
Melissa' website was a portal connecting all things related to the Melissa Brand. It had many feeds, connected with the brand social media and original content created at Transa.
The project was developed in Vanilla JS (with Prototype), CSS (Less) and PHP (Laravel).
The website also had a where to find, connected to the Google maps API listing all places where the brand can be found.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

sections: Com foco em sustentabilidade, o METCHA buscou ser carbono neutro. Usando técnicas modernas de entrega de conteúdo — redes distribuídas verdes como Cloudflare, divisão de código e carregamento progressivo — servíamos apenas o código necessário para a UI em tempo real, mantendo HTML 100% semântico para acessibilidade e SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

sections: In Nov. 2021 METCHA launched the METCHA FORWARD 2022 report, a page compiling over 500+ monthly pieces of content produced with a fresh blend of EXCLUSIVENESS in partnership with CREATIVE EXPONENTS after constant research performed by METCHA's multicultural digital native team.

The first METCHA FORWARDrelease is an analysis of behavioural movements that METCHA's team has been identifying over the last months. It compiles more than 20 global trends to guide the near future, covering all major leather industry-related categories.
I participated in the design of this page, with all team members, working especially close with Mia and Sagu for the layout.
Before, in the coding phase, I used Vue.js, Sass(CSS3) and Laravel(PHP/HTML5) to realize the designed layout and deliver the report by download.
I also worked with Renan Machado in the backend of the application.
In March of 2022, I also worked with METCHA's team helping to bring METCHA's content to GIPHY, a platform to increase METCHA's reach even more.

In less than a month METCHA's GIPHY channel gathered more than 4.6Milion views between METCHA's gifs and stickers, in a way to increase the organic reach of the project, on par with efforts like Bringing METCHA to Google News, and Google's discover page by applying many SEO techniques.

sections: Mini Melissa foi um projeto desenvolvido na Transa para o Grupo Grendene como canal dedicado à marca Mini Melissa.
O projeto durou de 2018 a 2020 e foi desenvolvido inteiramente com jQuery, CSS (Less) e PHP (Laravel).
O site tinha um feed de conteúdo e um feed social na página inicial, com rolagem infinita para conteúdo exclusivo da Mini Melissa.
A página 'onde encontrar' foi desenvolvida com a API do Google Maps como ponto central para localizar todas as lojas e clubes Mini Melissa no Brasil e no mundo.
Falando em coleções, confira algumas das coleções da Mini Melissa:

"Dance Machine", coleção Outono–Inverno 2016, desenvolvida com o candy framework, somente CSS e HTML.

"Flygrl", coleção Outono–Inverno 2017, desenvolvida com o candy framework, somente CSS e HTML.

"Mashup", coleção Primavera–Verão 2017, desenvolvida com o candy framework, somente CSS e HTML.

sections: Sage é um software fiscal desenvolvido pela Genesysinf, sediada em Santana do Livramento, Brasil.
Trabalhei na nova versão do Sageweb — desenvolvida em C# e ASP.NET — como desenvolvedor full-stack integrado à equipe por um ano.

O projeto consistia em portar o software Sage para desktop para uma nova versão web, com desafios como conectar drivers de impressoras fiscais à aplicação web, gerar e imprimir relatórios fiscais personalizados e criar uma interface similar à experiência desktop do Sage.

col1:
Hola, soy Luis —
Ingeniero de Software orientado a UX.
Actualmente trabajo en Dell en el Dell Design System.

Soy un profesional de TI con profunda experiencia en desarrollo web, análisis de sistemas y gestión de proyectos. Me especializo en crear soluciones digitales innovadoras y eficientes, con fuerte foco en SEO, accesibilidad y rendimiento. Mi repertorio técnico incluye ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript y SQL, junto con frameworks modernos como React, Vue y Angular.
col2: Estudié en la UFSM (Universidad Federal de Santa Maria) en Frederico Westphalen, Brasil, graduándome en Tecnología en Sistemas para Internet, con un posgrado en "Gestão de T.I" (Gestión de TI) en la UFSM.
Mi trabajo siempre está enfocado en entregar diseños pixel-perfect — código fácil de usar, rápido, hermoso y fluido.

Me encanta la animación en CSS. Pasé años creando las colecciones de temporada de Melissa casi íntegramente en CSS. Desde entonces he trabajado con animaciones JS usando Vue y Lottie, experimenté con Three.js y recientemente empecé a explorar el desarrollo orientado a especificaciones y la IA.

La edición de 2018 se tituló '¿Cuál es el retorno de la inversión sostenible?'.
La edición de 2019 se tituló 'El cuero en un mundo hiperconectado'.

I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2018' edition was called, 'Qual o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.

I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
2019' edition was called, 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

sections: Enfocados en la sostenibilidad, el proyecto METCHA buscó ser carbono neutral. Usando técnicas modernas de entrega de contenido — redes distribuidas verdes como Cloudflare, división de código y carga progresiva — servíamos solo el código necesario para la UI en tiempo real, manteniendo HTML 100% semántico.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

The first METCHA FORWARDrelease is an analysis of behavioural movements that METCHA's team has been identifying over the last months. It compiles more than 20 global trends to guide the near future, covering all major leather industry-related categories.

sections: Sage es un software fiscal desarrollado por Genesysinf, con sede en Santana do Livramento, Brasil.
Trabajé en la nueva versión Sageweb — desarrollada en C# y ASP.NET — como desarrollador full-stack integrado al equipo de desarrollo durante un año.

El proyecto consistía en portar el software de escritorio Sage a una nueva versión web, con desafíos como conectar drivers de impresoras fiscales a una aplicación web, generar e imprimir informes fiscales personalizados y construir una interfaz similar a la experiencia de escritorio de Sage.
sage.title: Genesysinf / Sageweb

col1:
Hallo, ich bin Luis —
Software-Ingenieur mit Fokus auf UX.
Ich arbeite derzeit bei Dell am Dell Design System.

Ich bin ein IT-Fachmann mit fundierter Expertise in Webentwicklung, Systemanalyse und Projektmanagement. Ich spezialisiere mich auf die Entwicklung innovativer, effizienter digitaler Lösungen mit starkem Fokus auf SEO, Barrierefreiheit und Performance. Mein technisches Repertoire umfasst ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript und SQL sowie moderne Frameworks wie React, Vue und Angular.
col2: Ich studierte an der UFSM (Bundesuniversität Santa Maria) in Frederico Westphalen, Brasilien, mit Abschluss in Technologie für Internetsysteme und einem Aufbaustudium in "Gestão de T.I" (IT-Management) an der UFSM.
Meine Arbeit ist immer darauf ausgerichtet, pixelgenaue Layouts zu liefern — Code, der einfach zu bedienen, schnell, schön und flüssig ist.

Ich liebe CSS-Animationen. Ich verbrachte Jahre damit, Melissas Saisonkollektionen fast vollständig in CSS zu gestalten. Seitdem habe ich JS-Animationen mit Vue und Lottie eingesetzt, mit Three.js experimentiert und begann kürzlich, spezifikationsgetriebene Entwicklung und KI zu erkunden.

sections: Brazilian Leather ist ein bei Transa entwickeltes Projekt in Partnerschaft mit CICB und Apex-Brasil.

2017 gab es eine neue Ausgabe: 'Kreislaufwirtschaft'.
Die Ausgabe 2018 trug den Titel 'Was ist die Rendite nachhaltiger Investitionen?'.
Die Ausgabe 2019 trug den Titel 'Leder in einer hypervernetzten Welt'.
2020 war eine Herausforderung — zwei Ausgaben wurden von Grund auf neu entwickelt: ein Online-Forum namens 'Leather Forward' und eine Präsenzveranstaltung.

2017 brought a new edition, 'Econômia Circular'.
It was developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2018' edition was called, 'Qual o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.
It was also developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for the CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
2019' edition was called, 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.
Developed using PHP, Jquery and CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/Subscription submitting of the application.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.
Both pages were developed using PHP, Sass for the CSS and Vanilla JS with code created from scratch exclusively for these new pages.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2021's edition brought a new challenge - creating the layout, and also coding the project.

sections: Melissa's website was a project developed by TRANSA INC.
I worked on the project from 2016 to 2020, when the project was ended.
Initially as a Jr. Front end Developer, guided by Cristiano Becker and ended as a Full Front End Developer by the end of the project.
Melissa' website was a portal connecting all things related to the Melissa Brand. It had many feeds, connected with the brand social media and original content created at Transa.
The project was developed in Vanilla JS (with Prototype), CSS (Less) and PHP (Laravel).
The website also had a where to find, connected to the Google maps API listing all places where the brand can be found.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

"À La Garçonne" was developed with many transitions in mind using the Symphony Framework, and lots of CSS.
"awaytomars" was a shorter page focused mainly on styling with CSS.
In "Satchel (CSC)" I worked mainly with the CSS, while Cristiano Becker focused on creating videos rendered in JS for the page to play on mobile.
In "Fabula" the focus was to bring the imagination to life, every single element of the page was animated in CSS by hand for desktop and mobile.

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

col1:
Hoi, ech bin de Luis —
Software-Ingenieur mit Fokus uf UX.
Arwed bei de Dell am Dell Design System.

Ech arwed schon lang mit Technologie — Webentwicklung, Systemanalyse un Projektmanagement. Ech mach gern effiziente digitale Lösung mit Fokus uf SEO, Zugänglichkeit un Performance. Ech haww schon mit ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript, SQL un moderne Frameworks wie React, Vue un Angular arwed.
col2: Ech haww an de UFSM (Universidade Federal de Santa Maria) in Frederico Westphalen studiert — Technologie in Internetsysteme, mit Postgraduierung in IT-Management, och an de UFSM.
Bei meine Arwed leg ech viel Wert druf, pixel-perfekte Layouts ze liefere — sauberer, schneller, schöner un flüssiger Code.

CSS un Animazioune sin schon immer mein Ding gewese. Ech haww jahrelang die saisonale Kollektioune vun Melissa fast komplett in CSS gemacht. Danach bin ech uf JS-Animazioune mit Vue un Lottie umgestiege, haww mit Three.js experimentiert un erforsch jetz specs-getriebene Entwicklung un KI.

sections: Brazilian Leather ist ein bei Transa entwickeltes Projekt in Partnerschaft mit CICB und Apex-Brasil.
Das Projekt ist ein Portal für brasilianisches Leder, das Websites wie Brazilian Leather, CICB, CSCB und Leather Law umfasst.
Bei Transa entwickelte ich außerdem eine Reihe von Landing Pages für das jährliche CICB Leather Forum.
2017 gab es eine neue Ausgabe: 'Kreislaufwirtschaft'.
Die Ausgabe 2018 trug den Titel 'Was ist die Rendite nachhaltiger Investitionen?'.
Die Ausgabe 2019 trug den Titel 'Leder in einer hypervernetzten Welt'.
2020 war eine Herausforderung — zwei Ausgaben wurden von Grund auf neu entwickelt: ein Online-Forum namens 'Leather Forward' und eine Präsenzveranstaltung.
Diese Ausgabe trug den Titel 'Unsere Umwelt in Verbindung'.
Ich erstellte das Layout auf Basis des vorherigen Layouts von Sagu bei Transa.
I contributed as a member of the team as a JR. Front-end developer, guided by Cristiano Becker on the development of this page in my first year at Transa.
2017 brought a new edition, 'Econômia Circular'.
It was developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2018' edition was called, 'Qual o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.
It was also developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for the CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
2019' edition was called, 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.
Developed using PHP, Jquery and CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/Subscription submitting of the application.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.
Both pages were developed using PHP, Sass for the CSS and Vanilla JS with code created from scratch exclusively for these new pages.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2021's edition brought a new challenge - creating the layout, and also coding the project.
This edition called:'Nosso ambiente em conexão'.
I created the webpage layout based on the previous layout created by Sagu, at Transa for the 2020 edition, keeping the already established visual identity.
The coding of the webpage was done in Vanilla JS, Sass(CSS3) and HTML5 only, with the use of lots of SVG elements in the layout of the page.

sections: Melissa's website was a project developed by TRANSA INC.
I worked on the project from 2016 to 2020, when the project was ended.
Initially as a Jr. Front end Developer, guided by Cristiano Becker and ended as a Full Front End Developer by the end of the project.
Melissa' website was a portal connecting all things related to the Melissa Brand. It had many feeds, connected with the brand social media and original content created at Transa.
The project was developed in Vanilla JS (with Prototype), CSS (Less) and PHP (Laravel).
The website also had a where to find, connected to the Google maps API listing all places where the brand can be found.

sections: Article pages were made to be a fluid experience.
Developed in a modal system, without refreshes, keeping the user on the same page with a beautiful pixel-perfect layout and smooth performance.
They consisted of articles, videos, and image galleries with original content created for Melissa's website.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

All with a unique look and feel to them.
Some of the collab pages I developed were, "À La Garçonne" Collab, "awaytomars", "Satchel (CSC)", "Fabula" and "Rider".
"À La Garçonne" was developed with many transitions in mind using the Symphony Framework, and lots of CSS.
"awaytomars" was a shorter page focused mainly on styling with CSS.
In "Satchel (CSC)" I worked mainly with the CSS, while Cristiano Becker focused on creating videos rendered in JS for the page to play on mobile.
In "Fabula" the focus was to bring the imagination to life, every single element of the page was animated in CSS by hand for desktop and mobile.
"Rider" was the last page bringing Melissa's sister "Rider" to the website.

Like Campana, Gaetano Pesce, J Maskrey, Gareth Pugh, Jason Wu, Jeremy Scott, Sebastian Errazuriz, Karl Lagerfeld, Vivienne Westwood, Vitorino Campos, Zaha Hadid and "Roller Joy" pages.
The improvements mainly consisted in adapting to new mobile device sizes, and CSS optimizations for every page, improving the load and render times.
Like the special and collab pages, many collections also had to be optimized and got some fixes.
Pages like "Cine Melissa", "Dance Machine", "Eat my Melissa", "Nation", "Starwalker", "Wanna be Carica" and "We are Flowers".

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

col1:
Hola, soy Luis —
Ingeniero de Software con foco en UX.
Trabajo en Dell en el Dell Design System.

Laburo en tecnología hace bastante — desarrollo web, análisis de sistemas y gestión de proyectos. Me gusta crear soluciones digitales eficientes, con foco en SEO, accesibilidad y performance. Trabajé con ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript, SQL y frameworks como React, Vue y Angular.
col2: Me recibí en la UFSM (Universidade Federal de Santa Maria) en Frederico Westphalen — RS, en Tecnología en Sistemas para Internet, con posgrado en Gestión de TI, también en la UFSM.
En el laburo me esfuerzo mucho por entregar layouts pixel-perfect — código limpio, rápido, lindo y fluido.

CSS y animaciones siempre fueron mi fuerte. Pasé años haciendo las colecciones de Melissa casi enteramente en CSS. Después me pasé a animaciones en JS con Vue y Lottie, jugué con Three.js y ahora estoy explorando desarrollo orientado a specs e IA.

sections: Brazilian Leather ist ein bei Transa entwickeltes Projekt in Partnerschaft mit CICB und Apex-Brasil.
Das Projekt ist ein Portal für brasilianisches Leder, das Websites wie Brazilian Leather, CICB, CSCB und Leather Law umfasst.
Bei Transa entwickelte ich außerdem eine Reihe von Landing Pages für das jährliche CICB Leather Forum.
2017 gab es eine neue Ausgabe: 'Kreislaufwirtschaft'.
Die Ausgabe 2018 trug den Titel 'Was ist die Rendite nachhaltiger Investitionen?'.
Die Ausgabe 2019 trug den Titel 'Leder in einer hypervernetzten Welt'.
2020 war eine Herausforderung — zwei Ausgaben wurden von Grund auf neu entwickelt: ein Online-Forum namens 'Leather Forward' und eine Präsenzveranstaltung.
Diese Ausgabe trug den Titel 'Unsere Umwelt in Verbindung'.
Ich erstellte das Layout auf Basis des vorherigen Layouts von Sagu bei Transa.
I contributed as a member of the team as a JR. Front-end developer, guided by Cristiano Becker on the development of this page in my first year at Transa.
2017 brought a new edition, 'Econômia Circular'.
It was developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2018' edition was called, 'Qual o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.
It was also developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for the CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
2019' edition was called, 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.
Developed using PHP, Jquery and CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/Subscription submitting of the application.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.
Both pages were developed using PHP, Sass for the CSS and Vanilla JS with code created from scratch exclusively for these new pages.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2021's edition brought a new challenge - creating the layout, and also coding the project.
This edition called:'Nosso ambiente em conexão'.
I created the webpage layout based on the previous layout created by Sagu, at Transa for the 2020 edition, keeping the already established visual identity.
The coding of the webpage was done in Vanilla JS, Sass(CSS3) and HTML5 only, with the use of lots of SVG elements in the layout of the page.

sections: Melissa's website was a project developed by TRANSA INC.
I worked on the project from 2016 to 2020, when the project was ended.
Initially as a Jr. Front end Developer, guided by Cristiano Becker and ended as a Full Front End Developer by the end of the project.
Melissa' website was a portal connecting all things related to the Melissa Brand. It had many feeds, connected with the brand social media and original content created at Transa.
The project was developed in Vanilla JS (with Prototype), CSS (Less) and PHP (Laravel).
The website also had a where to find, connected to the Google maps API listing all places where the brand can be found.

sections.label: Melissa - Where to find mobile tour

sections: Article pages were made to be a fluid experience.
Developed in a modal system, without refreshes, keeping the user on the same page with a beautiful pixel-perfect layout and smooth performance.
They consisted of articles, videos, and image galleries with original content created for Melissa's website.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

sections.label: Melissa - Color Me mobile collection tour
Melissa - Open Vibes mobile collection tour

sections: Collabs where short pages develop to show some of Melissa's collabs on the website.
All with a unique look and feel to them.
Some of the collab pages I developed were, "À La Garçonne" Collab, "awaytomars", "Satchel (CSC)", "Fabula" and "Rider".
"À La Garçonne" was developed with many transitions in mind using the Symphony Framework, and lots of CSS.
"awaytomars" was a shorter page focused mainly on styling with CSS.
In "Satchel (CSC)" I worked mainly with the CSS, while Cristiano Becker focused on creating videos rendered in JS for the page to play on mobile.
In "Fabula" the focus was to bring the imagination to life, every single element of the page was animated in CSS by hand for desktop and mobile.
"Rider" was the last page bringing Melissa's sister "Rider" to the website.

sections: Specials were short pages dedicated to special Melissa's products.
I worked by developed Melissa's "Bike" and Melissa's "Creatives" special pages, all done in Vanilla JS and CSS.
On the version 2.0 created in 2018 of the website, I also worked on improving many of the already existing collab and special pages.
Like Campana, Gaetano Pesce, J Maskrey, Gareth Pugh, Jason Wu, Jeremy Scott, Sebastian Errazuriz, Karl Lagerfeld, Vivienne Westwood, Vitorino Campos, Zaha Hadid and "Roller Joy" pages.
The improvements mainly consisted in adapting to new mobile device sizes, and CSS optimizations for every page, improving the load and render times.
Like the special and collab pages, many collections also had to be optimized and got some fixes.
Pages like "Cine Melissa", "Dance Machine", "Eat my Melissa", "Nation", "Starwalker", "Wanna be Carica" and "We are Flowers".
All with special care for the mobile layout and performance of these collections.

Such as the case of the "Gallerie"pages. Pages that showed melissas physical locations on the website.
Melissa's project was always creating something new, like the "Melissa Next" contest on UK and BR, and I coded the front end of both pages of the contest.

A page with lots of animations and graphic elements with a cool vibe to the approach of sustainability.
All the code was done in Vanilla JS and CSS only.

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

sections.title: Data Protection Rights
content: I want to make sure you are fully aware of your data protection rights. Every user is entitled to the following:
The right to access – You may request copies of your data. I do not store personal data; I'm happy to share any Google Analytics data if needed.
The right to rectification – You have the right to request correction of any information you believe is inaccurate, or to have incomplete information completed.
The right to erasure – You have the right to request that I erase your personal data, under certain conditions.
The right to restrict processing – You have the right to request that I restrict the processing of your personal data, under certain conditions.
The right to object to processing – You have the right to object to my processing of your personal data, under certain conditions.
The right to data portability – You have the right to request that I transfer any data I have collected to another organization, or directly to you, under certain conditions.
If you make a request, I have one month to respond to you. If you would like to exercise any of these rights, please contact me via email: luis.krotz@gmail.com.

content: Este documento está disponível em inglês. A versão em inglês é a versão juridicamente válida.

At luiskr, accessible from https://luiskr.com, one of my main priorities is the privacy of my visitors. This Privacy Policy document contains types of information that is collected and recorded by luiskr.com and how I use it.
If you have additional questions or require more information about my Privacy Policy, do not hesitate to contact me.

This Privacy Policy applies only to my online activities and is valid for visitors to my website with regards to the information that they shared and/or collect in luiskr.com. This policy is not applicable to any information collected offline or via channels other than this website.
By using my website, you hereby consent to my Privacy Policy and agree to its terms.
The personal information that you are asked to provide, and the reasons why you are asked to provide it, will be made clear to you at the point I ask you to provide your personal information.

If you contact me directly, I may receive additional information about you such as your name, email address, phone number, the contents of the message and/or attachments you may send us, and any other information you may choose to provide.

I use the information I collect in various ways, including to:
  1. Provide, operate, and maintain my website
  2. Improve, personalize, and expand my website
  3. Understand and analyze how you use my website
  4. Develop new products, services, features, and functionality
  5. Find and prevent fraud
  6. Log Files

luiskr.com follows a standard procedure of using log files. These files log visitors when they visit websites. All hosting companies do this and a part of hosting services' analytics. The information collected by log files include internet protocol (IP) addresses, browser type, Internet Service Provider (ISP), date and time stamp, referring/exit pages, and possibly the number of clicks. These are not linked to any information that is personally identifiable. The purpose of the information is for analyzing trends, administering the site, tracking users' movement on the website, and gathering demographic information. My Privacy Policy was created with the help of the Privacy Policy Generator and the Disclaimer Generator.

luiskr.com's Privacy Policy does not apply to other advertisers or websites. Thus, I'm advising you to consult the respective Privacy Policies of these third-party ad servers for more detailed information. It may include their practices and instructions about how to opt-out of certain options.

You can choose to disable cookies through your individual browser options. To know more detailed information about cookie management with specific web browsers, it can be found at the browsers' respective websites.
Under the CCPA, among other rights, California consumers have the right to:
Request that a business that collects a consumer's personal data disclose the categories and specific pieces of personal data that a business has collected about consumers.
Request that a business delete any personal data about the consumer that a business has collected.
Request that a business that sells a consumer's personal data, not sell the consumer's personal data.
If you make a request, I have one month to respond to you. If you would like to exercise any of these rights, please contact me.

sections: Brazilian Leather ist ein bei Transa entwickeltes Projekt in Partnerschaft mit CICB und Apex-Brasil.
Das Projekt ist ein Portal für brasilianisches Leder, das Websites wie Brazilian Leather, CICB, CSCB und Leather Law umfasst.
Bei Transa entwickelte ich außerdem eine Reihe von Landing Pages für das jährliche CICB Leather Forum.
2017 gab es eine neue Ausgabe: 'Kreislaufwirtschaft'.
Die Ausgabe 2018 trug den Titel 'Was ist die Rendite nachhaltiger Investitionen?'.
Die Ausgabe 2019 trug den Titel 'Leder in einer hypervernetzten Welt'.
2020 war eine Herausforderung — zwei Ausgaben wurden von Grund auf neu entwickelt: ein Online-Forum namens 'Leather Forward' und eine Präsenzveranstaltung.
Diese Ausgabe trug den Titel 'Unsere Umwelt in Verbindung'.
Ich erstellte das Layout auf Basis des vorherigen Layouts von Sagu bei Transa.
I contributed as a member of the team as a JR. Front-end developer, guided by Cristiano Becker on the development of this page in my first year at Transa.
2017 brought a new edition, 'Econômia Circular'.
It was developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2018' edition was called, 'Qual o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.
It was also developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for the CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
2019' edition was called, 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.
Developed using PHP, Jquery and CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/Subscription submitting of the application.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.
Both pages were developed using PHP, Sass for the CSS and Vanilla JS with code created from scratch exclusively for these new pages.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2021's edition brought a new challenge - creating the layout, and also coding the project.
This edition called:'Nosso ambiente em conexão'.
I created the webpage layout based on the previous layout created by Sagu, at Transa for the 2020 edition, keeping the already established visual identity.
The coding of the webpage was done in Vanilla JS, Sass(CSS3) and HTML5 only, with the use of lots of SVG elements in the layout of the page.

sections: Melissa's website was a project developed by TRANSA INC.
I worked on the project from 2016 to 2020, when the project was ended.
Initially as a Jr. Front end Developer, guided by Cristiano Becker and ended as a Full Front End Developer by the end of the project.
Melissa' website was a portal connecting all things related to the Melissa Brand. It had many feeds, connected with the brand social media and original content created at Transa.
The project was developed in Vanilla JS (with Prototype), CSS (Less) and PHP (Laravel).
The website also had a where to find, connected to the Google maps API listing all places where the brand can be found.

sections.label: Melissa - Where to find mobile tour

sections: Article pages were made to be a fluid experience.
Developed in a modal system, without refreshes, keeping the user on the same page with a beautiful pixel-perfect layout and smooth performance.
They consisted of articles, videos, and image galleries with original content created for Melissa's website.

sections.label: Melissa - Article:Ebulicao de cores e ideias

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

sections.label: Melissa - Color Me mobile collection tour
Melissa - Open Vibes mobile collection tour

sections: Collabs where short pages develop to show some of Melissa's collabs on the website.
All with a unique look and feel to them.
Some of the collab pages I developed were, "À La Garçonne" Collab, "awaytomars", "Satchel (CSC)", "Fabula" and "Rider".
"À La Garçonne" was developed with many transitions in mind using the Symphony Framework, and lots of CSS.
"awaytomars" was a shorter page focused mainly on styling with CSS.
In "Satchel (CSC)" I worked mainly with the CSS, while Cristiano Becker focused on creating videos rendered in JS for the page to play on mobile.
In "Fabula" the focus was to bring the imagination to life, every single element of the page was animated in CSS by hand for desktop and mobile.
"Rider" was the last page bringing Melissa's sister "Rider" to the website.

sections: Specials were short pages dedicated to special Melissa's products.
I worked by developed Melissa's "Bike" and Melissa's "Creatives" special pages, all done in Vanilla JS and CSS.
On the version 2.0 created in 2018 of the website, I also worked on improving many of the already existing collab and special pages.
Like Campana, Gaetano Pesce, J Maskrey, Gareth Pugh, Jason Wu, Jeremy Scott, Sebastian Errazuriz, Karl Lagerfeld, Vivienne Westwood, Vitorino Campos, Zaha Hadid and "Roller Joy" pages.
The improvements mainly consisted in adapting to new mobile device sizes, and CSS optimizations for every page, improving the load and render times.
Like the special and collab pages, many collections also had to be optimized and got some fixes.
Pages like "Cine Melissa", "Dance Machine", "Eat my Melissa", "Nation", "Starwalker", "Wanna be Carica" and "We are Flowers".
All with special care for the mobile layout and performance of these collections.

sections: I also played a role leading the front end team of the project in the late years of the project life-cycle, by guiding members of the Front end developer team in pages like "Baja East".
During the website life-cycle, many pages got updated and were constantly evolving.
Such as the case of the "Gallerie"pages. Pages that showed melissas physical locations on the website.
Melissa's project was always creating something new, like the "Melissa Next" contest on UK and BR, and I coded the front end of both pages of the contest.

A page with lots of animations and graphic elements with a cool vibe to the approach of sustainability.
All the code was done in Vanilla JS and CSS only.

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

The first METCHA FORWARDrelease is an analysis of behavioural movements that METCHA's team has been identifying over the last months. It compiles more than 20 global trends to guide the near future, covering all major leather industry-related categories.

sections: Brazilian Leather ist ein bei Transa entwickeltes Projekt in Partnerschaft mit CICB und Apex-Brasil.
Das Projekt ist ein Portal für brasilianisches Leder, das Websites wie Brazilian Leather, CICB, CSCB und Leather Law umfasst.
Bei Transa entwickelte ich außerdem eine Reihe von Landing Pages für das jährliche CICB Leather Forum.
2017 gab es eine neue Ausgabe: 'Kreislaufwirtschaft'.
Die Ausgabe 2018 trug den Titel 'Was ist die Rendite nachhaltiger Investitionen?'.
Die Ausgabe 2019 trug den Titel 'Leder in einer hypervernetzten Welt'.
2020 war eine Herausforderung — zwei Ausgaben wurden von Grund auf neu entwickelt: ein Online-Forum namens 'Leather Forward' und eine Präsenzveranstaltung.
Diese Ausgabe trug den Titel 'Unsere Umwelt in Verbindung'.
Ich erstellte das Layout auf Basis des vorherigen Layouts von Sagu bei Transa.
I contributed as a member of the team as a JR. Front-end developer, guided by Cristiano Becker on the development of this page in my first year at Transa.
2017 brought a new edition, 'Econômia Circular'.
It was developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2018' edition was called, 'Qual o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.
It was also developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for the CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
2019' edition was called, 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.
Developed using PHP, Jquery and CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/Subscription submitting of the application.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.
Both pages were developed using PHP, Sass for the CSS and Vanilla JS with code created from scratch exclusively for these new pages.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2021's edition brought a new challenge - creating the layout, and also coding the project.
This edition called:'Nosso ambiente em conexão'.
I created the webpage layout based on the previous layout created by Sagu, at Transa for the 2020 edition, keeping the already established visual identity.
The coding of the webpage was done in Vanilla JS, Sass(CSS3) and HTML5 only, with the use of lots of SVG elements in the layout of the page.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

The first METCHA FORWARDrelease is an analysis of behavioural movements that METCHA's team has been identifying over the last months. It compiles more than 20 global trends to guide the near future, covering all major leather industry-related categories.

Ciao, sono Luis —
Ingegnere del Software con focus su UX.
Lavoro in Dell nel Dell Design System.
col1:
Ciao, sono Luis —
Ingegnere del Software con focus su UX.
Lavoro in Dell nel Dell Design System.

Lavoro con la tecnologia da anni — sviluppo web, analisi di sistemi e gestione di progetti. Mi piace creare soluzioni digitali efficienti con focus su SEO, accessibilità e performance. Ho lavorato con ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript, SQL e framework come React, Vue e Angular.
col2: Mi sono laureato alla UFSM (Universidade Federal de Santa Maria) a Frederico Westphalen — RS, in Tecnologia per i Sistemi Internet, con specializzazione in Gestione IT, sempre alla UFSM.
Nel lavoro mi dedico molto a consegnare layout pixel-perfect — codice pulito, veloce, bello e fluido.

CSS e animazioni sono sempre stati il mio forte. Ho trascorso anni a creare le collezioni di Melissa quasi interamente in CSS. Poi sono passato ad animazioni JS con Vue e Lottie, ho sperimentato Three.js e ora sto esplorando lo sviluppo orientato alle specifiche e all'IA.

sections: Brazilian Leather ist ein bei Transa entwickeltes Projekt in Partnerschaft mit CICB und Apex-Brasil.
Das Projekt ist ein Portal für brasilianisches Leder, das Websites wie Brazilian Leather, CICB, CSCB und Leather Law umfasst.
Bei Transa entwickelte ich außerdem eine Reihe von Landing Pages für das jährliche CICB Leather Forum.
2017 gab es eine neue Ausgabe: 'Kreislaufwirtschaft'.
Die Ausgabe 2018 trug den Titel 'Was ist die Rendite nachhaltiger Investitionen?'.
Die Ausgabe 2019 trug den Titel 'Leder in einer hypervernetzten Welt'.
2020 war eine Herausforderung — zwei Ausgaben wurden von Grund auf neu entwickelt: ein Online-Forum namens 'Leather Forward' und eine Präsenzveranstaltung.
Diese Ausgabe trug den Titel 'Unsere Umwelt in Verbindung'.
Ich erstellte das Layout auf Basis des vorherigen Layouts von Sagu bei Transa.
I contributed as a member of the team as a JR. Front-end developer, guided by Cristiano Becker on the development of this page in my first year at Transa.
2017 brought a new edition, 'Econômia Circular'.
It was developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2018' edition was called, 'Qual o retorno do investimento sustentável?'.
It was also developed using PHP, Jquery and Less for the CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
2019' edition was called, 'O couro no mundo hiperconectado'.
Developed using PHP, Jquery and CSS.
I contributed as a Front end Developer and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/Subscription submitting of the application.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.
Both pages were developed using PHP, Sass for the CSS and Vanilla JS with code created from scratch exclusively for these new pages.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.
2021's edition brought a new challenge - creating the layout, and also coding the project.
This edition called:'Nosso ambiente em conexão'.
I created the webpage layout based on the previous layout created by Sagu, at Transa for the 2020 edition, keeping the already established visual identity.
The coding of the webpage was done in Vanilla JS, Sass(CSS3) and HTML5 only, with the use of lots of SVG elements in the layout of the page.

sections: Melissa's website was a project developed by TRANSA INC.
I worked on the project from 2016 to 2020, when the project was ended.
Initially as a Jr. Front end Developer, guided by Cristiano Becker and ended as a Full Front End Developer by the end of the project.
Melissa' website was a portal connecting all things related to the Melissa Brand. It had many feeds, connected with the brand social media and original content created at Transa.

The website also had a where to find, connected to the Google maps API listing all places where the brand can be found.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

sections: In Nov. 2021 METCHA launched the METCHA FORWARD 2022 report, a page compiling over 500+ monthly pieces of content produced with a fresh blend of EXCLUSIVENESS in partnership with CREATIVE EXPONENTS after constant research performed by METCHA's multicultural digital native team.

The first METCHA FORWARDrelease is an analysis of behavioural movements that METCHA's team has been identifying over the last months. It compiles more than 20 global trends to guide the near future, covering all major leather industry-related categories.
I participated in the design of this page, with all team members, working especially close with Mia and Sagu for the layout.
Before, in the coding phase, I used Vue.js, Sass(CSS3) and Laravel(PHP/HTML5) to realize the designed layout and deliver the report by download.
I also worked with Renan Machado in the backend of the application.
In March of 2022, I also worked with METCHA's team helping to bring METCHA's content to GIPHY, a platform to increase METCHA's reach even more.

In less than a month METCHA's GIPHY channel gathered more than 4.6Milion views between METCHA's gifs and stickers, in a way to increase the organic reach of the project, on par with efforts like Bringing METCHA to Google News, and Google's discover page by applying many SEO techniques.

about.frame:
Привет, я Луис —
Инженер-программист с фокусом на UX.
Работаю в Dell над Dell Design System.
col1:
Привет, я Луис —
Инженер-программист с фокусом на UX.
Работаю в Dell над Dell Design System.

Работаю в сфере технологий уже давно — веб-разработка, системный анализ и управление проектами. Люблю создавать эффективные цифровые решения с акцентом на SEO, доступность и производительность. Работал с ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript, SQL и фреймворками React, Vue и Angular.
col2: Окончил UFSM (Федеральный университет Санта-Марии) в Фредерику-Вестфален — RS, по специальности «Технологии интернет-систем», с постдипломом по управлению IT, также в UFSM.
В работе я большое внимание уделяю пиксельно-точным макетам — чистый, быстрый, красивый и плавный код.

CSS и анимации всегда были моей стихией. Я провёл годы, создавая сезонные коллекции Melissa практически целиком на CSS. Затем перешёл на JS-анимации с Vue и Lottie, экспериментировал с Three.js и сейчас изучаю разработку на основе спецификаций и ИИ.

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

sections: In Nov. 2021 METCHA launched the METCHA FORWARD 2022 report, a page compiling over 500+ monthly pieces of content produced with a fresh blend of EXCLUSIVENESS in partnership with CREATIVE EXPONENTS after constant research performed by METCHA's multicultural digital native team.

The first METCHA FORWARDrelease is an analysis of behavioural movements that METCHA's team has been identifying over the last months. It compiles more than 20 global trends to guide the near future, covering all major leather industry-related categories.
I participated in the design of this page, with all team members, working especially close with Mia and Sagu for the layout.

I also worked with Renan Machado in the backend of the application.
In March of 2022, I also worked with METCHA's team helping to bring METCHA's content to GIPHY, a platform to increase METCHA's reach even more.

In less than a month METCHA's GIPHY channel gathered more than 4.6Milion views between METCHA's gifs and stickers, in a way to increase the organic reach of the project, on par with efforts like Bringing METCHA to Google News, and Google's discover page by applying many SEO techniques.

Bonjour, je suis Luis —
Ingénieur logiciel avec une spécialisation en UX.

col1:
Bonjour, je suis Luis —
Ingénieur logiciel avec une spécialisation en UX.
Je travaille chez Dell sur le Dell Design System.

Je travaille dans la technologie depuis longtemps — développement web, analyse des systèmes et gestion de projets. J'aime créer des solutions numériques efficaces avec un focus sur le SEO, l'accessibilité et la performance. J'ai travaillé avec ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript, SQL et des frameworks comme React, Vue et Angular.
col2: J'ai obtenu mon diplôme à l'UFSM (Universidade Federal de Santa Maria) à Frederico Westphalen — RS, en Technologie des Systèmes Internet, avec un postdiplôme en Gestion IT, également à l'UFSM.
Dans mon travail, je m'investis beaucoup pour livrer des maquettes pixel-perfect — du code propre, rapide, beau et fluide.

CSS et animations ont toujours été ma spécialité. J'ai passé des années à créer les collections de Melissa presque entièrement en CSS. J'ai ensuite migré vers les animations JS avec Vue et Lottie, expérimenté Three.js et j'explore maintenant le développement piloté par les spécifications et l'IA.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

sections: Sage ist eine Steuersoftware von Genesysinf aus Santana do Livramento, Brasilien.
Ich arbeitete an der neuen Sageweb-Version — entwickelt in C# und ASP.NET — als Full-Stack-Entwickler im Entwicklungsteam für ein Jahr.

Das Projekt bestand darin, die Desktop-Software Sage auf eine neue Webversion zu portieren, mit Herausforderungen wie der Anbindung von Fiskaldruckertreibern an eine Webanwendung, der Generierung benutzerdefinierter Steuerberichte und dem Aufbau einer Oberfläche ähnlich der Sage-Desktop-Erfahrung.

Bon dì, mi me ciamo Luis —
Inzegner del Software, UX e tüto.
Laoro en Dell nel Dell Design System.
col1:
Bon dì, mi me ciamo Luis —
Inzegner del Software, UX e tüto.
Laoro en Dell nel Dell Design System.

Laoro con la tecnologia da tanto tempo — svilüpo web, analisi de sistemi e gestion de projeti. Me piass créar solussion digitài efisienti con fokus su SEO, acessibilità e performance. Ho laorà con ASP, PHP, C, C#, Pascal, Delphi, JavaScript, SQL e frameworks come React, Vue e Angular.
col2: Me son laureà a la UFSM (Universidade Federal de Santa Maria) a Frederico Westphalen — RS, en Tecnologia de Sistemi Internet, con pós-graduassion en Gestion IT, sempre a la UFSM.
Nel laoro me dedico tanto a consegnar layout pixel-perfect — codice neto, veloss, bèlo e fluido.

CSS e animassion i xe sempre stà el mio forte. Son stà ani a far le colession de Melissa quasi tüto en CSS. Po son passà a animassion JS con Vue e Lottie, ho sperimentà con Three.js e adesso esploro el svilüpo orientà a specs e IA.

I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/subscription submitting of the application.
