I contributed as a Front end Developer and worked closely with Renan Machado for the Back-end/Subscription submitting of the application.

2020' was a challenge with two editions created from scratch, an online edition of the forum called 'A sociedade somos todos nós' and a webinar called 'Leather business and the future consumer', in English and Portuguese.
Both pages were developed using PHP, Sass for the CSS and Vanilla JS with code created from scratch exclusively for these new pages.
I contributed as a Front end Developer, and worked with Renan Machado for the Back-end of the application.

sections: Melissa's website was a project developed by TRANSA INC.
I worked on the project from 2016 to 2020, when the project was ended.
Initially as a Jr. Front end Developer, guided by Cristiano Becker and ended as a Full Front End Developer by the end of the project.
Melissa' website was a portal connecting all things related to the Melissa Brand. It had many feeds, connected with the brand social media and original content created at Transa.
The project was developed in Vanilla JS (with Prototype), CSS (Less) and PHP (Laravel).
The website also had a where to find, connected to the Google maps API listing all places where the brand can be found.

sections: Every Melissa collection was designed to be a new experience for every season.
I developed the front end of many of them like, Color Me, Dreamers, Family, Flygrl, Mapping, Mashup, Mirror and Open Vibes, each with a unique feeling and experience.
"Color Me" was developed using the Symphony Framework for animations, created by Cristiano Becker for the project, it was all about a colourful experience.
"Dreamers" was an experience on its own, with use of the device camera to connect the user with the page.
"Family"had lots of transitions and animations and styled to bond with memories.
"Flygrl" was developed with lots of CSS only animations.
"Mapping" had an interactive experience with the use of the Google Maps API to search shoes in the collection of iconic locations.
"Mashup" was my first Melissa collection developed with Cristiano Becker, the first page to use the Symphony Framework to create animations.
"Mirror", developed with smooth text animations, especially on mobile.
"Open Vibes" was a collection with a mood from day to night, so we used SVGs and Canvas to achieve a day to night experience on scrolling.

"À La Garçonne" was developed with many transitions in mind using the Symphony Framework, and lots of CSS.
"awaytomars" was a shorter page focused mainly on styling with CSS.
In "Satchel (CSC)" I worked mainly with the CSS, while Cristiano Becker focused on creating videos rendered in JS for the page to play on mobile.

sections: Mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeit sollte METCHAs Projekt CO₂-neutral sein. Durch moderne Content-Delivery-Techniken — grüne Netzwerke wie Cloudflare, Code-Splitting und progressives Laden — lieferten wir nur den benötigten Code in Echtzeit, bei 100% semantischem HTML für Barrierefreiheit und SEO.
To adapt the project to international privacy rules we also developed a first-party 100% anonymous data collection tool for the project, called smart-data.

The main script contained a simple and very lightweight Javascript code to be initialized when the website is loaded. Then sending anonymous page views, that are stored and counted on the database, with the data sent from and to the API.

On the database, all daily data is gathered in a table without any information that can identify a user, 100% anonymous. At the end of the day, the table is consolidated and all the information is stored in a new table with a field to identify the event and the URL.

sections: To keep the information 100% anonymous, no user data is gathered and not even an ID is registered on the tables, all information collected is an URL of the website, a timestamp, the event name (page_view for example) and a value to attribute to the event like true or false, or an amount of time in seconds.

Then on METCHA's CMS, we create another script connecting to the API (PHP), and rendering via Javascript all the data in Numbers that make sense to the user, like the number of page views in a given interval of time, and creating some useful graphs like the session duration, which page had more clicks on a button, etc.

sections: Die MOR-Website wurde bei Transa entwickelt.

Das Ziel war ein schnelles und ansprechendes Erlebnis, das MORs Kanäle und Community an einem Ort verbindet.
Die kombinierte Größe von JS und CSS beträgt unter 50 KB für die gesamte Website — mit blitzschnellen Ladezeiten.

sections: Sage ist eine Steuersoftware von Genesysinf aus Santana do Livramento, Brasilien.
Ich arbeitete an der neuen Sageweb-Version — entwickelt in C# und ASP.NET — als Full-Stack-Entwickler im Entwicklungsteam für ein Jahr.

Das Projekt bestand darin, die Desktop-Software Sage auf eine neue Webversion zu portieren, mit Herausforderungen wie der Anbindung von Fiskaldruckertreibern an eine Webanwendung, der Generierung benutzerdefinierter Steuerberichte und dem Aufbau einer Oberfläche ähnlich der Sage-Desktop-Erfahrung.

Ich war Lead Front-End Developer und trug zum UX bis zur Fertigstellung des Projekts im Mai 2022 bei.

Die Website hatte viele einzigartige Seiten — darunter Transas Case Studies — die ich als Front-End-Developer leitete, umgesetzt im eigens entwickelten Content-Management-System von Transa, an dem ich ebenfalls mitentwickelte.
